protocol_type: Connection-oriented, frame-based serial protocol multiplexing three transports (SSP / STP / SMP) over a SAS phy. A port opens a connection with an OPEN address frame (carrying the destination SAS address, connection rate, protocol, and arbitration wait time); once OPEN_ACCEPTed, SSP/STP/SMP frames flow full-duplex with RRDY credit and ACK/NAK flow control, each protected by a 32-bit CRC, until CLOSE.

fis_format.framing: SOF primitive → FIS Dwords (FIS Type at byte 0) → 32-bit CRC → EOF primitive
fis_format.encoding: 8b/10b on the wire (defined in Serial ATA 2.6, not in AHCI)

fis_types.name: Register Host to Device (H2D)
fis_types.description: Carries ATA command; CFIS inside the Command Table is always H2D Register FIS.

fis_types.name: DMA Activate
fis_types.description: Device tells HBA it is ready to receive a Data FIS (write).

fis_types.name: DMA Setup
fis_types.description: Carries DMA buffer offset + transfer count + tag for first-party DMA / NCQ; copied into DSFIS.

fis_types.name: PIO Setup
fis_types.description: Carries Transfer Count + E_Status; copied into PSFIS.

fis_types.name: Set Device Bits
fis_types.description: Carries SActive update for NCQ completion; copied into SDBFIS; PxSACT bits clear here.

primitive_symbols.name: ALIGN
primitive_symbols.purpose: Clock-rate compensation; sent during link initialization and as fill primitive.

primitive_symbols.name: CONT
primitive_symbols.purpose: Indicates the following stream is a repeat of the previous primitive.

primitive_symbols.name: DMAT
primitive_symbols.purpose: DMA Terminate — host or device aborts a Data FIS in progress.

primitive_symbols.name: HOLD
primitive_symbols.purpose: Flow-control: transmitter run out of data.

primitive_symbols.name: R_RDY
primitive_symbols.purpose: Receiver ready for a new FIS.

primitive_symbols.name: WTRM
primitive_symbols.purpose: Wait Termination — sent after CRC + EOF to drain pipeline.

primitive_symbols.name: X_RDY
primitive_symbols.purpose: Transmitter ready to send a new FIS.

oob_signaling_sequence.name: COMRESET
oob_signaling_sequence.description: Burst of 4 ALIGN primitives + idle period, repeated.

oob_signaling_sequence.name: COMINIT
oob_signaling_sequence.description: Device response burst; informs host the device is present.

oob_signaling_sequence.name: COMWAKE
oob_signaling_sequence.description: Host acknowledgment burst; initiates speed negotiation.

oob_signaling_sequence.name: speed-negotiation
oob_signaling_sequence.description: Gen 1 (1.5 Gbps) → Gen 2 (3 Gbps) → Gen 3 (6 Gbps).

fields_dw0.name: CFL
fields_dw0.description: Command FIS Length in Dwords (2..16; 0/1 illegal).

fields_dw3.name: CTBAU
fields_dw3.description: Command Table base address upper 32 b.

prd_entry_format.name: DBC
prd_entry_format.description: Data Byte Count (zero-based, max 4 MB / entry).

channels.name: TX (A+ / A-)
channels.description: Outbound differential pair; 8b/10b at Gen 1/2/3 line rate.

valid_ready_handshake_rules: Framing by SOF / EOF primitives + 32-bit CRC.
X_RDY ↔ R_RDY primitive handshake gates each FIS start.
HOLD / HOLDA provides Dword-level flow control inside Data FIS.
Software flow control is PxCI[slot] set→clear; HBA clears on completion.

frame_format.cfis: Command FIS — H2D Register FIS, up to 16 Dwords (64 B).
frame_format.rfis: Received D2H Register FIS, 20 B, copied to RFIS region.
frame_format.data_fis: Data FIS — 1 Dword header (Type 0x46) + N Dwords payload up to 8 KB.

transport_protocols.name: SSP
transport_protocols.purpose: Transport SCSI commands, task management, data, and status between SAS initiator and target ports.

transport_protocols.name: STP
transport_protocols.purpose: Tunnel SATA FIS across the SAS domain to SATA devices behind expanders via an STP/SATA bridge.

transport_protocols.name: SMP
transport_protocols.purpose: Discover and configure the SAS topology at expander SMP target ports (request/response).

ssp_frame_types.name: COMMAND
ssp_frame_types.purpose: Carries a SCSI Command Descriptor Block (CDB).

ssp_frame_types.name: XFER_RDY
ssp_frame_types.purpose: Target-to-initiator transfer-ready; flow control for write data.

ssp_frame_types.name: RESPONSE
ssp_frame_types.purpose: Carries SCSI status and sense data.

connection_management.open: OPEN address frame: source SAS address, destination SAS address, requested connection rate, protocol (SSP/STP/SMP), arbitration wait time (AWT).
connection_management.arbitration: Expanders route the OPEN frame and emit AIP (Arbitration In Progress) while arbitration resolves contention by arbitration wait time.
connection_management.accept_reject: Destination replies OPEN_ACCEPT (open) or OPEN_REJECT (reject: no destination, pathway blocked, bad destination, retry).
connection_management.close: CLOSE closes an open connection; BREAK aborts a connection or connection request; DONE ends frame transmission.
connection_management.rate_matching: ALIGN (and NOTIFY) primitives are inserted when the connection rate is slower than the physical link rate.

primitive_descriptions.name: ALIGN
primitive_descriptions.use: Dword synchronization, rate matching, clock skew management.

primitive_descriptions.name: NOTIFY
primitive_descriptions.use: Signals events (e.g. ENABLE SPINUP, power loss expected).

primitive_descriptions.name: SOF / EOF
primitive_descriptions.use: Start / End of Frame delimiters for SSP/SMP frames.

primitive_descriptions.name: RRDY
primitive_descriptions.use: Receiver Ready — grants one frame of credit.

primitive_descriptions.name: BREAK
primitive_descriptions.use: Abort a connection or connection request.

primitive_descriptions.name: DONE
primitive_descriptions.use: End the current connection's frame transmission.

addressing.note: Each port has a 64-bit SAS address (NAA worldwide name); connections are addressed by source/destination SAS address in the OPEN address frame.

crc.coverage: SSP and SMP frame contents (frame header + information unit).
crc.scrambling: Data dwords (excluding primitives) are scrambled by a linear-feedback scrambler.

flow_control.credit: RRDY grants one frame of credit; CREDIT_BLOCKED signals no credit.
flow_control.ack_nak: ACK acknowledges and NAK negative-acknowledges an SSP frame (NAK triggers retransmission).
